author: GuardianNigeria
title: 2027: Civil Society Groups Warn Against Partisan Academics as Election Officials
text:
The Resource Centre for Human Rights & Civic Education (CHRICED) and the Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) are concerned about the potential appointment of politically biased academics as returning and collation officers in the 2027 general elections. The groups argue that the recent mobilisation of senior academics by a political party creates a conflict of interest that undermines the integrity of the electoral process.
The Resource Centre for Human Rights & Civic Education (CHRICED) has raised the alarm over emerging indications that vice chancellors, professors and senior university lecturers with clear, recent partisan political involvement may be deployed as returning and collation officers in the 2027 general elections.
The Human Rights Writers Association of Nigeria (HURIWA) has echoed these concerns, warning that the use of traditional and religious institutions for partisan endorsements compromises their neutrality. CHRICED, in a statement signed by Executive Director Ibrahim Zikirullah, stressed that the integrity of an election depends on the demonstrable independence and impartiality of its officials.
The centre is particularly troubled by a recent media report alleging that more than 600 senior academics from public universities in the North attended a closed-door meeting in Kaduna convened by an All Progressives Congress (APC) chieftain. This meeting was explicitly aimed at securing the endorsement and active support of academics for President Bola Tinubu's 2027 re-election bid.
CHRICED argues that if individuals who have publicly taken partisan positions are assigned to collate or declare election results, a clear conflict of interest arises, threatening public confidence in the electoral process. HURIWA, in a statement by its National Coordinator Emmanuel Onwubiko, criticised the deployment of high-profile institutions for partisan campaigns, specifically citing the endorsement of Tinubu by the Lagos and Benin monarchs.
The group insists that while citizens have the right to support candidates, the use of institutions with significant public influence as platforms for partisan endorsements compromises their credibility and moral authority. Both organisations are urging the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to prevent the inclusion of politically biased academics in the electoral administration to ensure the 2027 election is free, fair, and trustworthy.
